sections.label: Purpose of Ministerial Statement
sections.summary: The statement reiterates the fundamentals of the approach to race, religion and language and its political application.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The purpose of this Ministerial Statement is to reiterate the fundamentals of our approach to race, religion and language, and its application in the political context.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, the background to our approach to race, language and religion.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, recent incidents where race and religion were brought into politics.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And third, why if we go down this path, it will lead to bad outcomes for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Majority language and culture norm
sections.summary: In 1965, the norm worldwide was that the majority's language and culture became the state's.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Many such practices and arguments over race, language and religion were quite common.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Thus, in 1965 when Singapore became independent, whether you looked at Asia, Africa, Americas or Europe, the norm was that the language and culture of the majority would automatically become the language and culture of the state.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew independence declaration
sections.summary: Lee Kuan Yew declared Singapore was not a Malay, Chinese or Indian nation, with equal place for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew declared on the day of our Independence: “This is not a Malay nation; this is not a Chinese nation; this is not an Indian nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Everyone will have his place, equal: language, culture and religion.” This was not just political rhetoric.

sections.label: English and mother tongues in schools
sections.summary: English was the language of administration and instruction, while students studied mother tongues as a second language.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: English was used as the language of administration and instruction, meaning the language used in schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At the same time, students studied their mother tongues – Mandarin, Malay, Tamil – as a second language.

sections.label: Malay as national language
sections.summary: Malay was retained as Singapore's national language.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At the same time, we retained Malay as our national language.

sections.label: Parliament seats after 1963 GE
sections.summary: Their foothold in Parliament was eroded to 25 out of 51 seats at the 1963 GE.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Their foothold in Parliament had been eroded to just 25 out of 51 seats at the time of the 1963 GE, less than half.

sections.label: Council, racial harmony laws
sections.summary: The Council assesses whether legislation disadvantages racial or religious groups, reports to Parliament, and laws set out disallowed conduct and speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Council's function is to assess whether any legislation would create a differentiating measure which would disadvantage any racial or religious group more than others.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Council's report would then be tabled in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Laws were also passed to set out what conduct, what speech would not be allowed relating to race, religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And over time we have been strengthening, modernising these laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have for example, the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act, Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These laws set out the ways in which we can deal with threats to racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: Hate speech disallowed
sections.summary: Hate speech and offensive speech against races and religions are disallowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, we disallow hate speech and offensive speech, against races and religions.

sections.label: Legal framework and public discussion
sections.summary: A legal framework protects communities' rights and sets out what cannot be done or said publicly, with a calibrated approach to public discussion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One, a robust legal framework that protects the rights of all communities and sets out what you cannot do, what you cannot say in public; and two, a reasonable, calibrated approach to discussing such views in public as well.

sections.label: Promoting intermixing and understanding
sections.summary: The Government should actively promote actions and platforms encouraging intermixing and understanding between different communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is where the second key policy framework comes in.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This second key policy is that the Government should actively promote actions, platforms to encourage intermixing and understanding between our different communities.

sections.label: Survey and police report figures
sections.summary: Surveys show high ratings for racial and religious harmony, and 178 police reports on race and religion were filed over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the 2023 Gallup World Poll, 92% of Singaporeans said that Singapore was a good place for racial and ethnic minorities and we ranked first out of 135 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the 2024 Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) Survey on race, religion and language, 65% of Singaporeans rated racial and religious harmony as high or very high.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the past five years, there have been 178 Police reports filed relating to race and religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This works out to only about three cases per 100,000 people per annum.

sections.label: Dangers of identity politics
sections.summary: The Government highlighted that identity politics sways voters for short-term gain but sows hard-to-contain division that would irretrievably damage Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In these cases, the Government highlighted the dangers of identity politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is an easy way to sway the emotions of voters for short-term political gain, but once the division has been sown, it is hard to contain and impossible to reverse.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If this happens in a small diverse city state like Singapore, we will be irretrievably damaged.

sections.label: Edelman Trust Barometer global survey
sections.summary: The Edelman Trust Barometer's annual global survey found more than half of respondents say their countries are more divided today than in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Edelman Trust Barometer conducts a large-scale global survey every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They found that more than half of the respondents globally say that their countries are more divided today than in the past.

sections.label: Financial industry GDP contribution
sections.summary: The financial industry contributes 14% of gross domestic product.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The financial industry contributes to 14% of our gross domestic product (GDP).

sections.label: Voting along racial religious lines
sections.summary: Asking Singaporeans to vote for political parties and candidates along racial religious lines is reckless.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Asking Singaporeans to vote for political parties and candidates along racial religious lines is a reckless thing to do.

sections.label: PAP Malay-majority seats 1963
sections.summary: In the 1963 General Election, after Singapore became a constituent state in Malaysia, the PAP won all three Malay-majority seats.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the 1963 GE, after we became a constituent state in Malaysia, the PAP won all three Malay-majority seats in Singapore at that time – Geylang Serai, Kampong Kembangan and Southern Islands.

sections.label: Othman Wok called kafir
sections.summary: Encik Othman Wok, the leading Malay leader in the PAP then, was called a kafir, and within 10 months came the July 1964 riots.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The leading Malay leader in the PAP then, Encik Othman Wok, was called a "kafir".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And within 10 months, we got the riots of July 1964.

sections.label: Joint statement religion politics dangers
sections.summary: On 25 April, MHA and ELD released a joint statement highlighting the dangers of mixing religion and politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 25 April, my Ministry, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Elections Department (ELD) released a joint statement highlighting the dangers of mixing religion and politics.

sections.label: Rejecting race and religion in politics
sections.summary: He called on Singaporeans to reject race and religion in politics and asked parties to stand on two principles; the WP statement said no deals were made to Deros.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He called on Singaporeans to reject efforts to bring race and religion into politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He asked all political parties to take a clear stand on two principles: one, that identity politics has no place in Singapore; and two, that we should never mix religion and politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The WP statement stated that no promises, commitments or agreements were made to Deros in exchange for political support.

sections.label: WP statement on Deros
sections.summary: The statement did not categorically reject Deros' call to Muslims to vote along racial and religious lines, nor his support for Faisal Manap.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The statement did not categorically reject Deros' call on Muslims in Singapore to vote along racial, religious lines, nor did it reject Deros' support for its anchor in Tampines, Mr Faisal Manap.

sections.label: Timing of WP statement
sections.summary: Other words conveying the same points could have been used, but it should have been stated squarely right after Deros' 23 April statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Any other form of words, conveying the same points, could also have been used.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But it should have been squarely stated immediately after Deros issued his statement on 23 April, without letting the matter drag.

sections.label: PAS support and MHA-ELD statement
sections.summary: PAS leaders openly supported a political party on racial and religious grounds during a GE, the party had not responded, so the MHA-ELD statement was issued and access disabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When the PAS leaders openly supported a political party in Singapore on racial and religious grounds and in the middle of a GE, and when the political party in question had not responded.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, the MHA-ELD statement I referred to earlier, was issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Access to the posts by the PAS politicians was disabled.

sections.label: PM on foreign influence
sections.summary: The Prime Minister called on all political parties to make their stand clear on foreign influence and reject foreign endorsements of their candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Prime Minister called on all political parties to: one, make their stand clear on foreign influence; and two, clearly and categorically reject foreign endorsements of their candidates.

sections.label: WP statement on foreign influence
sections.summary: On the substance, the WP statement did not clearly reject foreign influence or the foreign endorsement of its candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the substance, the WP statement did not clearly reject foreign influence, or the foreign endorsement of its candidates.

sections.label: Singh rejects foreign involvement
sections.summary: Mr Singh said he categorically rejected any foreign involvement in Singapore's domestic politics and that WP needs no foreign support.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Then, finally, at a rally speech later that evening, which took place after the Prime Minister's press conference, Mr Singh went further and gave the WP's clearest statement on the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said that he categorically rejected the involvement of any foreign elements whatsoever in Singapore's domestic politics; and two, that WP does not need the support of any foreign element.

sections.label: Damanhuri Abas racial appeals
sections.summary: SDP candidate Mr Damanhuri Abas sought support along racial lines, accusing PAP Malay MPs of failing the Malay community and urging Malay voters against the PAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Damanhuri Abas was a Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) candidate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He had made attempts to get support along racial lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At an SDP event, Mr Damanhuri accused the PAP Malay MPs of failing to represent the Malay community and ignoring their issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In an interview posted on social media, Mr Damanhuri stated that Malay community issues had not been resolved for 60 years under PAP rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He called for the Malay voters to vote against the PAP, framing it as an issue of upholding Malay dignity.

sections.label: Religion not for politics
sections.summary: Religion must not be misused for political purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Religion must not be misused for political purposes.

sections.label: Foreign countries may influence politics
sections.summary: Without a firm stand, foreign countries watching the GE may be tempted to play on ethnic sympathies, and all major communities can be externally influenced.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Through the course of this speech, I have explained why that will be bad for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is obvious – if we do not take a firm stand, some foreign countries, including those not in our immediate neighbourhood, who must have been watching our GE very carefully, will be tempted to play on ethnic sympathies to influence our politics; and all our major communities are capable of being influenced from external sources.

sections.label: Ministerial Statement purpose and fundamentals
sections.summary: The Ministerial Statement sets out fundamentals and how politicians and parties should conduct themselves, urging responsible handling of race and religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The main purpose of this Ministerial Statement is to set out: one, our fundamentals on which I hope there will be agreement; two, a clearer understanding on how we hope politicians and political parties will conduct themselves in future should these issues arise again.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As Parliamentarians, we may debate and disagree on many things, but I hope that we can all commit to handle issues of race and religion in a responsible and sensible manner, and to uphold the integrity of Singapore's secular politics.

sections.label: Deros and Damanhuri went too far
sections.summary: In the recent GE, Deros and Mr Damanhuri have gone too far.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the recent GE, Deros, Mr Damanhuri, have gone too far.

sections.label: Malay land offer rejected
sections.summary: Tunku Abdul Rahman asked Johor to set aside 10 acres for Malays leaving Singapore, but no Pioneer Generation Malay took up the offer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the very day Mr Lee Kuan Yew pledged that this will not be a Malay nation, Chinese nation, Indian nation, and that all will be equal, then-Malaysian Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman said that he had asked the Johor State government to set aside 10 acres of land for any Malay in Singapore who wished to leave the newly independent country.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You might think that it might have appeared an attractive option to some of our Pioneer Generation of Malays – get some land and remain a member of the majority in Tanah Melayu.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But not a single Pioneer Generation Malay took up the offer.

sections.label: Minister asked for concise answers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to keep answers clear and concise, noting the Minister raised timing of the WP's response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I would also similarly ask the Minister to also keep his answers clear and concise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It appears to me that one of the issues the Minister raises is with regard to timing, in terms of how quickly the WP responded to some of the issues the Minister covered in his Statement.

sections.label: Politicisation of public space
sections.summary: The speaker says politicising the public space is unhealthy for Singapore and minority communities, and notes the joint MHA-ELD statement was published on 25 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think once we go down that road, you're going to have an unnecessary politicisation of the public space and we don't want that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That's not healthy for Singapore and that's not healthy for our minority communities as well." On the matter of timing, the joint MHA-ELD statement was published on 25 April.

sections.label: WP statement timing dispute
sections.summary: The WP released its statement on 26 April at 9.30 am, followed by a doorstop interview, so the speaker disagrees it took too long.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 26 April, the following morning, at 9.30 am, the WP releases its statement, overnight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At 11.30 am or thereabouts, there is a doorstop interview and one of the remarks that I made include what I have just mentioned, as the preamble to this clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, on the matter of timing, I do not agree with the Minister that we took too long.

sections.label: Questions on Noor Deros legality
sections.summary: The speaker says it is unfair to claim the WP did not take the issue seriously and asks whether Noor Deros broke laws or faced a police report or restraining order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I do not think it is fair to say that the WP did not take this issue seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also would like to clarify – did Noor Deros break any laws?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Was a Police report made against him, or was it in the Government's contemplation to issue a restraining order against him under section 8 of the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act?

sections.label: Deros met WP Malay candidates
sections.summary: Deros said he met all the WP's Malay candidates, posted on 23 and 24 April, and would canvass support for the WP if it agreed to his demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: According to Deros, he met with all of the WP's Malay candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Assume that was known, Deros put up his posts on 23 and 24 April, Nomination Day and the second day.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Deros talked about his meeting with the WP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said he would canvas support for the WP, if the WP agreed to his demands and said that people should vote for Mr Faisal Manap, and this was after meeting Mr Faisal Manap and the WP's Malay candidates.

sections.label: WP statement on Deros
sections.summary: The WP statement of 26 April did not reject Deros' position on racial and religious voting or his support for Faisal Manap.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The statement was issued on 26 April, the WP statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I said earlier, it did not reject Deros' position that he would ask Muslims in Singapore to vote along racial and religious lines, nor did it reject Deros' support for its anchor in Tampines, Mr Faisal Manap.

sections.label: Government statement approach
sections.summary: The Government decided to issue a statement through MHA and ELD and then make this Ministerial Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As for the past, the Government decided to take the approach that it has done, which is to issue a statement through MHA and ELD, and then make this Ministerial Statement.

sections.label: Streisand effect and Deros
sections.summary: Raising the matter may bring greater focus to points made by Noor Deros, who later accepted WP did not agree with him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Streisand effect – by raising the matter, are you actually, in the heat of an election, bringing the issue to greater focus?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, by dealing with it on 23 or 24 April, points made by a certain Noor Deros, who really no one knows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: He later on, on 6 May, accepts that WP did not agree to anything that he said.

sections.label: Deros meeting WP leaders
sections.summary: Mr Singh agrees it could have been clearer; the person meeting Deros was the WP Vice Chairman with all WP Malay candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On Deros, I think listening to Mr Singh, he agrees that it should have been and could have been clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And let us just remember the person meeting Deros was the Vice Chairman of the party, a CEC member, a very senior leader, he was meeting Deros together with all the WP Malay candidates.

sections.label: PM public statement during GE
sections.summary: The Prime Minister made an extraordinary move and spoke in public during the GE, saying this is not acceptable.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Prime Minister made an extraordinary move because it was so important, and he came out and spoke in public during the GE, and said this is not acceptable.

sections.label: PAS and Deros endorsements
sections.summary: PAS endorsing PAP candidates of any race would be rejected; Deros and PAS endorsed WP's Malay/Muslim candidates, leading to identity politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If PAS had endorsed the PAP candidates of any race, I think this House, knowing as it does our philosophy, can be sure that we will have rejected it immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One is Deros' endorsement of WPs' Malay candidates, leading clearly into an identity politics situation; and the other, PAS' endorsement of WPs' Malay/Muslim candidates.

sections.label: Reaching out to political parties
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government's perspective is broader than a small political party and that clarification could be sought from all political parties as one Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Government has a perspective which is far broader than a small political party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And my point is, if it is serious enough, in the Minister's words, for the Prime Minister to take measures such as stopping campaigning halfway to clarify a point, I do not think it is too difficult to reach out in the national interest to get that clarification also from all political parties as one Singapore.

sections.label: Asymmetry of information with WP
sections.summary: The speaker says WP had all the information because neither the Government nor the PAP met Mr Deros, and only knows what he reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If there is any asymmetry of information, it is that WP had all the information because neither the Government nor the PAP met with Mr Deros.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Until today, I do not know what was said.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I only know what he reports as having been said and I know that nothing has been said by WP about what transpired other than that no promises, commitments or agreements were made.

sections.label: Rejection of PAS interference
sections.summary: The speaker says that even with the asymmetry of information, the matter is not acceptable, and Mr Singh issued a clear rejection of PAS' interference.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And even with that asymmetry of information, knowing what we did, it strikes us and it seems to me to strike anyone, that this is not acceptable.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if it is not acceptable, for example Mr Singh issued a clear and unequivocal rejection of PAS' interference.

sections.label: MHA-ELD statement and PM
sections.summary: The speaker says the statements were clear but carefully drafted, and the Prime Minister decided to come out and say it because it is fundamental for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the statements were clear, but carefully drafted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is the MHA-ELD statement and the Prime Minister decided to come out and say it because this is fundamental for Singapore.

sections.label: PM brought up Noor Deros
sections.summary: The speaker says the only official Government mention was when the Prime Minister brought up Noor Deros, and that same night they made their position clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The only time it came up officially from the Government was when the Prime Minister brought Noor Deros up specifically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But as the Prime Minister made his press conference, this was on 26 April at around noon-ish; same night, we made our position very clear on needing support from individuals on racial and religious grounds.

sections.label: WP statement on religion and politics
sections.summary: The speaker says the WP statement dealt with religion and politics and said no agreements, commitments or promises had been made.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In response, the WP statement dealt with religion and politics, and said no agreements, commitments or promises had been made.

sections.label: Rejecting demands at meeting
sections.summary: The speaker says demands were rejected when they met him, and the wording should have said so.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think Mr Singh has said yes, it could have been clearer, instead of just saying no agreements, promises or commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It should have said we reject his demands; we rejected it when we met him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I hope his demands were rejected when there was the meeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We rejected his demands when we met him.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community as victim
sections.summary: The Malay/Muslim community was a victim of these tactics during this general election.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our Malay/Muslim community during this GE was a victim of these tactics.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim community stayed calm
sections.summary: The Malay/Muslim community stayed calm despite deliberate attempts to rile up racial and religious sentiments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Malay/Muslim community has stayed calm in spite of the deliberate attempts to rile up racial and religious sentiments among the community.

sections.label: Identity politics targeting Chinese community
sections.summary: The speaker says one thrust of the speech is that identity politics will lead everyone to target the Chinese community.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In fact, one thrust of my speech is that if we go down this road of identity politics, everyone will be targeting the Chinese community for obvious reasons.

sections.label: Constitutional special position of Malays
sections.summary: The commitment dates to pre-Independence and the Constitution recognises the special position of Malays and the Government's responsibility for their interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It dates back to pre-Independence, to the days of Mr Lee Kuan Yew, and successive Prime Ministers have reiterated this fundamental commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why our Constitution recognises the special position of Malays.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It states that it shall be the responsibility of the Government to protect, safeguard, support, foster, promote their political, educational, religious, economic, social and cultural interest, and the Malay language.

sections.label: Call to vote along racial lines
sections.summary: The speaker says the man's call for Malay/Muslims to vote along racial and religious lines was troubling and would ruin Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He is entitled to his opinions, ideas and suggestions, regardless of how absurd these were.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But what was troubling was his call for Singaporean Malay/Muslims, to vote along racial and religious lines for specific candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The largest groups will be the ones that all political parties will cater to.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And that will be the road to Singapore's ruin.

sections.label: Timing of raising concerns
sections.summary: A Member asks why the concerns are raised now rather than earlier, noting the Minister sought the earliest opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the Minister has mentioned earlier that he was looking for the earliest opportunity to bring this up and also was mindful about being seen as threatening smaller political parties, could the Minister help us understand why are we raising these concerns now, in particular, and not back then?

sections.label: Earliest opportunity after PM intervention
sections.summary: The reply states this is the earliest opportunity after the Prime Minister's intervention, and it was decided Parliament should deal with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: After the Prime Minister's intervention in the Debate on President's speech, this is the earliest opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We decided that it should be dealt with in Parliament.

sections.label: Serious view and stiff charging
sections.summary: The Minister says the matter is taken very seriously, is not acceptable, and will be dealt with stiffly in charging and Government decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members would have heard me say that we take this very seriously; it is not acceptable.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And we will deal with it very stiffly in terms of the charging position that we take and decisions that are taken from the Government side.

sections.label: Do not attack religions or races
sections.summary: The request is not to attack other religions or races, as that breaches the law, which will be enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: All we ask is: first of all, do not attack other religions or races, because that will breach the law and we will enforce the law.

sections.label: Legislation protecting minorities employment
sections.summary: Within that framework, discrimination and racism need not be accepted, and legislation now protects minorities from wrongful employment termination including for race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And within that framework, it does not mean that you must accept discrimination, you must accept racism.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And in fact, recently, legislation has been put in place that protects minorities and others from having their employment terminated for the wrong reasons, including that of race or religion.

sections.label: Foreigners favouring WP not interference
sections.summary: Citing foreigners who favour the WP does not amount to being within the definition of interfering with local politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We can cite various people who favour the WP who are foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That does not amount to being within the definition interfering with our local politics.

sections.label: Foreign political articles censorship position
sections.summary: The speaker invites the WP to state whether it would support censoring all foreigners' political articles on Singapore and taking down all their posts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I ask the Member not to put words in my mouth.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I would say I would invite the WP to tell me – would they take the position that we ought to be censoring and objecting to every article on politics in Singapore by any foreigner and would that apply to all the international journals?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If Mr Tiong's position is that, and that we should similarly take down all posts by any foreigner, and if we put forward legislation to that effect, if WP would support it, then we will talk about it.

sections.label: Strengthening civic education against racial politics
sections.summary: The speaker asks how public awareness and civic education can be strengthened so Singaporeans recognise and reject racially or religiously motivated influence attempts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: And I believe that harmony comes from confidence and trust and sometimes, not avoiding difficult conversations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, beyond calling out and effecting the law in response to potential attempts to influence voting behaviour along racial and religious lines, how can we strengthen public awareness and civic education to help our Singaporeans recognise and reject such messages, so that they do not become victims of politically motivated individuals?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The first is, to do what we have done up to now, eschew race-based politics in the mainstream, do our best and what we do every weekend, go down to the ground as MPs, have events which bring in all the different races together.

sections.label: Standing firm against race card
sections.summary: The speaker says that when the race or religious card is played, they must be clear and stand firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The second is when there are attempts to play the race card or the religious card, I think we have to be clear and we have to stand firm, which is why I said, it would have been far easier for me not to make the Statement and just move on.

sections.label: IPS 2024 racial and religious harmony survey
sections.summary: The speaker cites the IPS 2024 survey where 65.4% rated racial and religious harmony high or very high, noting perception gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his speech, he referred to one of the policy pillars being our reasonable calibrated approach to discussing such views in public, referring to religious issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I want to refer to the Minister's citing of the IPS 2024 survey on racial and religious harmony and the headline statistic in Annex C, where it is stated that 65.4% of respondents rated Singapore's racial and religious harmony is high or very high, and this is on the uptrend from the last time the survey was run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of course, this is a heartening statistic, but there is some nuance to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That same report highlighted that there was a perception gap between what the Chinese majority felt versus minorities, quite a significant one, as well as a perception gap between the younger generation and the older generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Those 35 and below felt that racial and religious harmony was worse than the older respondents.

sections.label: Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act
sections.summary: The passage states that there is the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You have the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act.

sections.label: Keeping racial and religious harmony acts
sections.summary: The speaker says nothing stops others from organising such events, but the answer is not to do away with the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act or Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And as I said earlier, there is nothing to stop Mr Low or anyone else from organising more of such on their own terms, as long as they do not insult any race or religion and hopefully, they will encourage people to be more respectful.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But the answer is not to do away with the Maintenance of Racial Harmony Act or Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act.

sections.label: WP response to Deros endorsement
sections.summary: WP rejected passes, overtures and endorsements through Pritam Singh's rally speech, and said it made no commitments, promises or agreements on Deros.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: WP never rejected Deros' views, I think, never rejected his endorsement, never rejected him saying, "Vote for Mr Faisal Manap over Minister Masagos." WP rejected passes, overtures and endorsements through Mr Pritam Singh's rally speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On Deros, the most that was said was that we made no commitments, promises or agreements.

sections.label: Deros endorsement not rejected
sections.summary: Deros' endorsement on the basis of race and religion was not rejected during the last GE, and WP said it did not know who he was.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Deros' endorsement on the basis of race and religion was not rejected during the last GE.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We hope that going forward, it will be rejected unequivocally and immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What was done was to say, we do not know who he is, you know, he is a nobody, and we have made no promises, agreements or commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And Mr Singh knows what a rejection sounds like, because he was clear and unequivocal after the Prime Minister called for a clear rejection.

sections.label: Meeting with Aljunied mosque member
sections.summary: A Muslim committee member in an Aljunied mosque wanted to speak to Faisal and Malay party members at a meeting with ulama.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: What had happened was that one of our Muslim committee members in one of the mosques in Aljunied wanted to speak to Mr Faisal and to the Malay members of the party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And what happened was that the meeting was supposed to take place with some ulama, some senior Malay/Muslim religious leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: There was no indication that this individual would be joining in the meeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, when the meeting started, he was there, and my understanding is he had this list of demands.

sections.label: Rejection of Deros' advocacy
sections.summary: Government officials and Ministers meet various religious group members, and the speaker says the gentleman is mistaken if he thinks his advocacy will be brought up by WP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I think Government officials, even Ministers, meet with various members of religious groups in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And if this gentleman thinks that his advocacy will lead to the issues being brought up by the Workers’ Party, I think he is sadly mistaken." Sir, in my view, that is a rejection of what Mr Deros is trying to put forth.
